result.title: The Value of Not Knowing: How Fresh Eyes through Naive LLMs Fuel Creativity
result.summary: Many major scientific advances come from approaching a problem with a new or novel perspective. While large language models (LLMs) with internet-scale knowledge seem poised to take such perspectives, their consistent generation remains elusive. Instead, models are drawn to dominant views and preexisting, in-field bias. To explore the potential of fresh eyes to increase creativity, this paper proposes naive LLMs, models that are made intentionally ignorant of a specific topic. Through deprivation in training or intentional forgetting, naive models are unburdened by existing dogma, allowing them to be free to make new associations and conjectures. These naive models can then be paired with a stronger mentor model that can refine their unique perspectives into concrete proposals. For the 1B and 7B models tested in this paper, naive models consistently produce seed ideas that are more novel and useful than baseline counterparts, and mentor refinement improves the ideas even further. Thus, contrary to the prevailing tradition of scaling up training data, we demonstrate a case where less information is actually more powerful, in particular when the aim is to discover genuinely outside-the-box solutions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「naive LLM」：通过训练期知识剥夺或定向遗忘，让模型对某一主题保持无知，以摆脱领域内主流观点；再与更强的 mentor 模型配对，把其新奇的种子想法细化为具体方案，并在 1B/7B 模型上报告种子想法更新颖、更有用。
AI.relevance_reason: 刻意削减模型知识可视为人为控制内部知识状态的手段，可能供核查 latent 推理中先验主导与假设多样性之间的权衡；种子想法加 mentor 精炼的两段式流程，也与候选 latent 状态的提出—筛选—验证结构有概念上的可借鉴之处。
